idiom_name: make_<product>(kind) with a dict / if-chain dispatch
implementation_notes: Python's classes are callables and its modules are namespaces, so the classic abstract Creator collapses into a module-level function that consults a mapping (or an if/elif chain) and calls the chosen class - the shape dict.fromkeys and datetime.fromisoformat show in the standard library. Because a function is not obliged to construct anything, it can return a cached instance, a subclass, or raise a domain error for an unknown key; a Protocol or ABC is only needed when the product's own interface must be enforced.
pitfalls: A dict registry keyed by an unvalidated string turns a typo into a KeyError deep in the call stack; validate keys at the boundary (Literal, Enum) and raise a domain error listing valid keys.
Module-level registries are process-wide mutable state: tests that register types leak into other tests unless registration is scoped or the table is reset in a fixture.
Returning different concrete types from one function defeats type checkers' narrowing; annotate the return as the Protocol/ABC (or use overloads) so mypy/pyright still enforce the interface.

variants.name: @classmethod alternate constructor (cls(...))
variants.implementation_notes: The most common factory in Python is a @classmethod that computes the constructor's arguments and ends in `return cls(...)`: docs.python.org notes that a class method receives the class as an implicit first argument, so a subclass calling the factory gets its own type back with no override. Use it when the variation is how inputs are interpreted (from_iso8601, from_dict, from_row) rather than which class is built.
pitfalls: Hard-coding the class name instead of using cls(...) silently returns the base type for subclasses - the one mistake this idiom exists to prevent.
A classmethod is inherited by every subclass, including ones for which the input format is meaningless; document or guard the precondition.
__init__ cannot return a different instance (it must return None); when the chosen class depends on the input, use __new__ or a plain factory function instead.

variants.name: __init_subclass__ self-registration consumed by a lookup
variants.idiom_name: ABC with __init_subclass__ registering cls in a ClassVar registry
variants.implementation_notes: __init_subclass__ (PEP 487) runs on the parent whenever a subclass is created, so each concrete class can register itself at definition time and the factory becomes a table lookup - adding a product is adding a class, with no edit to existing code. The classic Creator subclass is still the tool when subclassing is already part of the design; self-registration is for open-ended sets of implementations spread over several modules.
pitfalls: Registration happens when the module defining the subclass is imported, so a plugin that nothing imports never registers - import plugin modules eagerly (the registry is filled by import side effects).
Name the registry explicitly as Shape.registry rather than cls.registry: cls.registry resolves through the MRO and a subclass that defines its own table silently registers nowhere the factory looks.
An intermediate abstract class registers too, so make() can hand out a non-instantiable class; filter abstract classes or require an explicit key.
